_why: ceo's ruling 2026-09-08: 'a workflow change outside its owner's lane reached main through a pipeline you own without you refusing it.' A lane is who may CHANGE a path, which is a different question from owned-path-facts.json's (what a change to a path must DECLARE) -- so it is a separate file with a separate owner. Data, so ceo can move a lane without touching scripts/workflow-lane-check.mjs, and so the mechanism cannot quietly decide who owns what.
_exception: A lane is not a wall. ceo assigns across lanes deliberately -- #548 was ceo's assignment to the PM, in ceo's words, and the PM asked first. The exception is a line in the PR body, and it is PRINTED by the check rather than merely accepted, so a deliberate crossing is in the log rather than in somebody's memory. See the Lane-exception format in the script's header. AND THE BOUNDARY ITSELF MUST BE RIGHT FIRST: a generated file belongs to its generator's owner, and an exception is for a deliberate crossing of a CORRECT boundary, never for a wrong one. ceo, 2026-09-09, after `.github/workflows/` as a flat prefix would have refused #558 -- whose author flagged it before pushing rather than routing around it. Asking them to write a Lane-exception for a mis-stated rule would have been the guard-people-route-around failure this exception exists to prevent, arriving one door along.

lanes.why: trunk health and the merge queue. Owner moved from dispatcher to ceo on 2026-09-11 (#913): dispatcher was retired in the Org Reset of 2026-09-10, and a lane whose owner no longer exists refuses every PR with a message nobody can act on. Until #902 removes this check with the mergeSafety job, an engineer's pipeline change is assigned per PR by a Lane-exception line naming ceo. trunk health and the merge queue. A workflow edited by a session that is not watching the queue is a red check nobody owns -- measured 2026-09-08, when a pull_request trigger attached a failing audit to seven merged PRs and sat red for ninety minutes before anyone in the org read the view the chairman reads. revert/ is here because trunk-guard's own decideRevert opens those branches and they carry whatever the reverted commit touched.
lanes.exceptWhy: A GENERATED file whose SOURCE lives outside the lane is not the lane's to own. consumer-gate.yml is regenerated from README.md by scripts/generate-consumer-gate.mjs, so its content is contract work that happens to land in this directory -- the pipeline does not decide what it says, and the cost of changing it is visible from the generator's seat rather than from the merge queue, which is the whole test for whether a path belongs to a lane. Added 2026-09-09 after the flat prefix would have refused #558 and forced its author to write a Lane-exception for a rule that was mis-stated: making somebody paper over a wrong rule with a body line is the guard-people-route-around failure the exception was designed to prevent, arriving one door along.
